title: The Qt Object Model: Signals and Slots

questions.question: Why should a battery monitor emit a signal instead of calling the screen directly?
options: Because signals are faster than function calls
So the warning can be delayed until the screen is ready
So the monitor does not depend on the screen, the logger, or anything else
Because Qt forbids calling functions between classes
questions.explanation: Emitting inverts the dependency. The monitor announces, listeners subscribe, and the monitor stays testable and reusable on a robot with no screen.

questions.question: What does the moc tool do?
options: It checks that your signals have matching slots
It reads headers containing Q_OBJECT and generates the signal and connection code
It links Qt libraries into your program
It compiles QML into C++
questions.explanation: moc is the meta object compiler. It writes the bodies of your signals and the metadata that lets connect find them at runtime.

questions.question: Three things are needed for a Qt class to work. Which is NOT one of them?
options: It must contain the Q_OBJECT macro
Its header must be known to the build system so moc sees it
It must inherit from QObject
The class must be allocated with new rather than on the stack
questions.explanation: Stack allocation is fine, and often preferable. What moc needs is the inheritance, the macro, and a header it is actually given.

questions.question: Why does the monitor use two thresholds rather than one?
options: Because battery percentages are never exact
So the signal can carry two values
Because Qt requires a matched pair of signals
A reading sitting on a single threshold would emit a storm of warnings as it flickers
questions.explanation: That gap is hysteresis. It converts a noisy crossing into a single, meaningful state change, and every real threshold detector has one.

questions.question: You get undefined reference to vtable for BatteryMonitor. What is wrong?
options: moc did not run for that class, because of a missing Q_OBJECT or a header the target does not know about
The signal has the wrong argument type
Qt is not installed
You forgot to call connect
questions.explanation: Without moc, the generated virtual functions and signal bodies do not exist, so the linker has nothing to point the vtable at.

questions.question: What is the equivalent of signals and slots in ROS 2?
options: Topics, which are publish and subscribe by another mechanism
Services, which are request and response
Parameters, which store configuration
Actions, which manage long running goals
questions.explanation: A publisher announces on a topic and subscribers receive. The transport is completely different, the decoupling idea is the same one you just used.
